content.value_statement: Many Rust codebases hide failures behind panics or vague errors. This skill reviews patterns and suggests idiomatic Result, thiserror, and anyhow improvements.
actual_capabilities: Identifies unwrap, expect, and panic usage in Rust error handling.
Suggests Result and Option propagation with the ? operator.
Recommends typed library errors with thiserror.
Recommends anyhow context for application-level failures.
Explains automatic error conversion with From and #[from].
Highlights tests for expected error cases.
limitations: Focuses on Rust error handling, not general application architecture.
Provides review guidance and examples, not formal verification.
Does not run builds, tests, or benchmarks by itself.
Needs user-provided code context to make precise recommendations.

use_cases.title: Remove Panic Paths
use_cases.description: Find production unwrap, expect, and panic usage and convert failures into recoverable errors.

use_cases.title: Design Library Errors
use_cases.description: Create specific error enums that preserve source errors and support clear caller handling.

use_cases.title: Review Error Quality
use_cases.description: Check pull requests for missing context, broad error variants, and untested failure cases.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Error Handling
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small Rust function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rust function for unwrap, expect, panic, and missing Result handling. Explain the safest simple improvement.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Error Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Add useful context to application errors.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rust workflow and suggest where anyhow context would make failures easier to debug.

prompt_templates.title: Design Typed Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these library errors and suggest a thiserror enum with specific variants and preserved source errors.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Error Boundaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across application and library boundaries.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Rust module for error propagation, conversion, caller ergonomics, and tests for important failure cases.

output_examples.input: A function loads configuration with expect and then reads a file with unwrap.
output: Flags both calls as panic risks in production code.
Suggests returning a Result from the function.
Adds context so callers know whether configuration or file loading failed.

output_examples.input: A library returns string errors from validation functions.
output: Recommends a typed validation error enum.
Explains how callers can match specific error cases.
Suggests tests for empty input, invalid format, and length limits.

output_examples.input: A pull request manually maps database errors into generic messages.
output: Notes that the original database error is lost.
Suggests preserving the source error through automatic conversion.
Recommends adding caller-facing context at the application boundary.

best_practices: Return Result from fallible functions instead of panicking in reusable code.
Use thiserror for library error types and anyhow for application boundaries.
Test expected failure cases, not only successful paths.
anti_patterns: Using unwrap or expect in production paths without a clear invariant.
Returning generic string errors that callers cannot match safely.
Dropping source errors during manual conversion.

faq.question: What languages does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Rust error handling patterns and Rust ecosystem crates.

faq.question: Can it choose between thiserror and anyhow?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends thiserror for libraries and anyhow for application-level context.

faq.question: Does it remove every unwrap automatically?
faq.answer: No. It reviews context and suggests changes when a panic path is risky.

faq.question: Can it help with tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests tests for expected error variants and important failure paths.

faq.question: Does it execute Rust code?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides review guidance and needs separate tools to run builds or tests.

faq.question: Is it useful for libraries and applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives different recommendations for reusable libraries and application entry points.
